sourceReview.note: Three batches: all six decks (274 slides); 17 workbook files checked. The 16 new files supply both lab problem sets, the descriptive lab answers, workbook answer variants, standalone examples and four reports. Report methods and key confidence-interval tables were examined from their full extracted text.

lessons.title: Fundamental concepts and descriptive statistics
lessons.intro: Start with the statistical unit and measurement scale, then describe the centre, spread, shape and association in healthcare data.
outcomes: Classify variables and choose an appropriate graph
Calculate and interpret centre, spread and outlier fences
Distinguish association from a causal effect

lessons.title: Sampling methods, random variables and probability distributions
lessons.intro: Connect sampling design to probability models, expected values, normal standardisation and the Student’s t table.
outcomes: Interpret probability mass, density and cumulative probability
Standardise a normal measurement and find t percentiles
lessons.source: Topic 2, slides 1–64; Exercise Book 2026/27, exercises 13–28; Statistical Tables, tables D.1 and D.2.

lessons.title: Point estimation of the population mean and variance
lessons.intro: Understand why an estimator varies across samples, how standard error measures precision, and why variance estimation uses n−1.
outcomes: Connect sampling distribution, bias and precision
Choose the adjusted variance and explain its denominator
lessons.source: Topic 3, slides 1–33; Understanding Notation; Exercise Book 2026/27, exercises 29–32.

lessons.title: Confidence intervals for the population mean and proportion
lessons.intro: Build a point estimate plus a margin of error, choose z or t correctly, and write a confidence statement that matches the target.
outcomes: Construct mean intervals with known or unknown variance
Construct and check a proportion interval
Explain repeated-sampling coverage and interval width
lessons.source: Topic 4, slides 1–33; Formula Sheet; Exercise Book 2026/27, exercises 33–50.

lessons.title: Hypothesis tests for one population mean and proportion
lessons.intro: Work from hypotheses to a test statistic, p-value and decision, then explain what the result means in healthcare.
outcomes: Specify two-sided null and alternative hypotheses
Choose the correct mean or proportion test SE
Interpret p-values without claiming proof of equality
lessons.source: Topic 5, slides 1–36 (reviewed 7 October 2026); Formula Sheet; Exercise Book 2026/27, exercises 51–60; mock-answer document Q7–Q9. The guide uses the current book numbering; the slide exercise ranges are older. Type II error/power and the proportion counterexample are clearly labelled supplementary context.

lessons.title: Comparison of two population means
lessons.intro: Recognise independent and paired designs, calculate the uncertainty of a difference and interpret a two-group result.
outcomes: Identify an independent or paired comparison
Interpret effect direction, p-values and significance legends
lessons.source: Topic 6, slides 1–29; Exercise Book 2026/27, exercises 61–64. Additional topic in the syllabus, time permitting.
